newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX breach 2,800 level in post-bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German DAX breach 2,800 level in post-bourse trade.

text.p: German shares travelled further into record territory on Friday, with the share index even managing to breach the 2,800-point threshold in late electronic trade.

Dealers said trade was underpinned by a record close on Wall Street overnight and the strength of the dollar, adding that it augured well for the giant flotation of Deutsche Telekom, Germany's telecoms incumbent, due Monday.

"This is very good, coming just before the Telekom flotation on Monday. The market is favouring different sectors in turn -- chemicals, utilities, cars and now the banks. This is a very healthy bull market," a Frankfurt trader said.
The DAX index had earlier closed at 2,795.80 points, up 18.79 points or 0.68 percent after reached an intraday high of 2,799.05 points.
The IBIS DAX index closed at 2,800.60 points, 16.21 points up on the day, after earlier reaching a high of 2,803.31.
The surge is the latest push-forward in a largely U.S.-inspired rally that has seen the DAX index progress from barely above the 2,500-point mark since September.

The three biggest German banks were among the heaviest-traded stocks in Frankfurt over the course of bourse trade as traders focused on banks amid speculation about mergers and takeovers within the sector.

Commerzbank AG started bourse trade higher, but the price was hit by profit-taking over the session and it ended bourse trading down five pfennigs at 36.60 marks. Nearly three million Commerzbank shares changed hands over floor trade.
Dresdner Bank AG ended up 30 pfennigs at 44.70 marks, while Deutsche Bank AG ended up 15 pfennigs at 72.35 marks.
Electronics group Siemens AG was among the session losers, ending down 26 pfennigs at 73.64 marks.
Dealers said the group was suffering after profit warnings in its passive components and electron tubes division on Thursday and the generally poor outlook for the German electronics sector.
